title: Pawcam: what the dog does at 2pm

product.name: Pawcam
product.one_liner: pet camera with a treat tosser and two-way audio, works over home wifi

audience: people 25-45 who work outside the home and leave a dog alone during the day

presenter.description: fictional woman, early forties, office lanyard, phone in hand; generated, not based on anyone

hook.why: Opens a question the viewer has asked themselves; the footage answers it.

style: split between office phone footage and living-room camera feed, daylight, candid

shots.visual: Camera-feed view: an empty sofa, then a dog's nose appears over the cushion
shots.camera: fixed wide, slightly fisheye, like a pet cam
shots.caption:
what the dog does at 2pm

prompt.subject: wide fisheye view of a living room sofa from a low shelf, a brown dog's nose and eyes rising over the cushion
prompt.action: the dog's head rises slowly over the back of the sofa and stares at the lens
prompt.setting: living room, daytime, curtains half drawn
prompt.camera: fixed wide, slight fisheye, low shelf height

shots.visual: Presenter at an office desk checking her phone, worried; she mouths 'is he okay'
shots.caption: eight hours of wondering
shots.voiceover: You leave at nine and spend the day wondering if he's fine, bored, or eating the sofa.

prompt.subject: fictional woman in her early forties with an office lanyard at a desk, glancing at her phone with a worried look
prompt.action: she checks the phone, frowns, puts it down, picks it up again

shots.visual: Screen recording of the app: live feed opens in two taps, presenter talks, the dog's ears go up
shots.camera: screen capture with the live feed
shots.caption: two taps. he hears you.
shots.voiceover: Two taps and you're looking at him. Say his name and the ears go up.

shots.visual: Camera-feed view: a treat flies out, the dog catches it off the sofa
shots.caption: treat button. he forgives you.
shots.voiceover: Hit the treat button. He forgives you for leaving.

prompt.subject: wide fisheye view of the living room, a small brown treat arcing from the bottom of the frame, the brown dog leaping off the sofa to catch it
prompt.action: the treat arcs out, the dog jumps and catches it mid-air, tail wagging
prompt.negative: extra treats, extra dogs, text, timestamp

shots.visual: Real product on a shelf, hand points at the treat hopper and the microphone grille; the setup screen shows it joined home wifi
shots.caption: hopper, mic, wifi. no hub.
shots.voiceover: Treat hopper, microphone, speaker. Plugs in, joins your wifi, no hub.

shots.visual: Presenter at her desk, phone turned to show the dog asleep on the sofa
shots.caption: see what yours does at 2pm. link below.
shots.voiceover: See what yours does at two. Link below.

prompt.subject: the fictional woman at her office desk turning her phone to the lens, a dog asleep on a sofa visible on the screen

notes: The pet-cam feed shots are generated and labelled; the real device appears in shot 5 so the hardware shown is the hardware shipped.
No separation-anxiety or veterinary wording; the ad sells reassurance for the owner, not a treatment for the dog.
Generated feed has no timestamp overlay so it cannot be mistaken for a real recording of a real home.
